reviews.text: 简单来说，Dice A Million就是骰子版本的《小丑牌》。玩家通过商店、通关奖励来构筑自己的骰子阵容，用各种被动效果搭配出尽可能变态的“卡组”，来获取尽可能高的分数。本作与《小丑牌》的一个不同点在于，本作包含了一些剧情元素，所以玩家是可以打出“真结局”，或者说是可以“通关”本作的。 本作的汉化全部由我完成。汉化出现错漏的可能性很大，主要是由以下原因造成的： 1. 我翻译的时候打哈欠了。 2. 我翻译的时候肚子饿了。 3. 我太菜了根本通不了关，导致游戏后期的汉化内容没有在游戏里进行测试。 4. 我汉化水平太低。 朋友们在游玩过程中如果发现汉化有错漏之处，还请在该评测的评论区、该游戏的讨论区，或是在b站为我指路。非常感谢！

Dice A Million is Numbers go Up roguelike perfected. The run diversity is insane, there are so so so many potentially viable builds (I KNOW I can make marbles work) and there are plenty of unlockables hiding under the surface. Not to mention there are rumblings of some pretty interesting secrets even just one complete win in. Having a well functioning build and earning a billion pips in a single roll feels like someone applied dopamine directly to my entire brain. The dice feel good. The music sounds good. The unlocking is good. This game is so good.

Played the Demo and got addicted, and now I'm loving all the polish and new stuff added in the full version. Obviously the game's visuals take heavy inspiration from Balatro, but it does a lot of things in an interesting and unique way, so calling it "Balatro with dice" would be unfair. There are a lot of well thought out game design decisions that make the game very rewarding to play. For example, your score on a certain stage and currency are one in the same, meaning if you have a busted combination of dice scoring you 10x what you need, whatever isn't paid off at the end of the level goes into your pocket, giving you much more money to spend in the shop and rewarding you for over-scoring. Similarly, any unspent currency contributes to the next stage's score requirement, meaning you can give yourself an easier time next level by holding off on spending. The game has a load of fun builds you can spec into, and great synergies and anti-synergies between dice and rings (passive effects). For example, a lot of dice release an area of effect around themselves, adding or multiplying value to other dice in that radius. The magnetic dice pulls dice together, and the Red Giant gains permanent value every time it finds itself in an area of effect. Build your dice bag around this, and you can get crazy value from one dice. There are also dice that do nothing when initially rolled, but gain "charge" such that after a certain number of rolls triggers a powerful effect, like creating a legendary dice, or rolling a copy of every single dice on the table. That last one is fun because half of the time you forget that its fully charged, roll it, and suddenly a chain of random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ starts rolling repeatedly and suddenly there are 50 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dice on the table and you just scored 12M points when you only needed 5000. Sound design is also super satisfying and crunchy, and the music is great. Only complaint I have (which was from the Demo, so it may be changed now) is the Eye of God legendary ring (which lets you choose 1 dice to guarantee rolling its highest face) feels a bit underpowered, since a lot of the more powerful dice have a negative effect if they roll their highest face. Can't tell you how many times I've used this ring on a D666, forgetting that this dice destroys itself if it lands on 666. That may very well just be a skill issue on my part, and there are probably more dice worth using this ring on in the full version. If you enjoyed Balatro you'll probably get the same dopamine hits from insane synergies here, and if you're not sure there's always the demo.

I'll start by saying I like this game a lot. It has a lot of fun die and ideas, very addictive. The presentation and humor is great. But I can't fully recommend it as it currently is. When it comes to the game itself, there is frankly a lot of bs that makes the game unfun and frustrating when you feel like you got your build figured. For example there is a Boss called "The Patient", During this boss fight you are not allowed to use your dice until they've been played once. So guess what happens when on the previous stage you get a crazy good amount of currency and have +70 dice in your inventory? You are just screwed and removing dice becomes pointless as it becomes expensive very quickly. There are other bosses that also completely negate certain builds to the point I question why even have certain die or marbles in the game if in long term leads to a guaranteed loss. I agree with the reviews saying the Bosses need tuning and that the RNG is too much. Its a terrible feeling to think you have something just to hit a brick wall for what seems like a reasonable build.

[h2]Now with even more obnoxious bosses!![/h2] The number one complaint about the demo was that most bosses were way over the top and completely unbalanced. Unless you were running a very specific, niche build, they were practically impossible to beat. So what did the developer do for the full release?! Exactly! He made them [i]even more unbalanced[/i] and [i]obnoxious.[/i] [spoiler][b]LA-DI-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-DA![/b][/spoiler] You cannot make this ♥♥♥♥ up, ladies and gentlemen. I'm still recommending it because honestly, at this price range, even with all the problems, it's still an absolute steal. But damn, I wish this game were more about "haha, big numbers go bigger" instead of forcing you to completely tailor your playstyle for a specific boss, only to get your ass handed to you on a silver tray by the next one. But hey, maybe that's just me.

大概2/29内容 游戏可以，数值极其的烂，在各种逆天数值机制改之前不推荐，第四层加强boss女巫运气不好会直接毁灭整个长线，各种boss不仅有对短线还有对长线的干扰，以及彻底摧毁某个阵容或者运气不好直接瘫痪全部牌组的boss，同时你无法跳过战斗导致有的时候还要硬吃依托大的，诅咒还会覆盖掉附魔导致长线崩溃 一二三层boss有几个会影响和摧毁卡组的boss非常恶心，其他都还可以，如果只是想打一到三层的话随便玩还是推荐的 接下来是针对四五层的了，四五层压力极大，转型几乎不可能，运气不好还会碰上导致崩盘的boss 红色房间清除附魔里包括常青，这会导致下一回合无法继续叠加附加值 如果筹码直接够数值可以跳过房间并获取奖励，这点类似小丑牌，但问题是我跳过时还跳过了一个商店，那我都付出筹码了我还跳过商店自讨苦吃吗，但战斗内又不能直接交钱又要硬生生丢好多次骰子拖时间，干吗啊这是 附加值和顶面数值的关系解释不清晰 有针对附加值打法的对策boss，有针对骰子点数的boss，还有专门破坏卡组的boss，还有拼爆发和拼长线的对策，并且一轮下来会吃5个boss导致极其容易碰上对策或毁灭长线的boss 骰子有低概率丢出范围内，应该是bug 哦对，由于点击后是没有二次确认的，因此如果你点击速度太快非常容易误操作 模仿者+会沉默整回合吗，推荐用词改为"丢出重复顶面后对应骰子的特殊效果这轮不会再触发"不比"特殊效果不会触发"好多了吗，以及四五层的增强头目几乎就没一个不被针对的流派的 很神奇的是，附加值拥有翻倍软上限，明显这是不想让附加值出现无限翻倍叠加的情况，需要去磨倍率，这一步本身问题不大，真正的问题是倍率叠加骰子数量不足，有部分为范围性叠加，有部分为概率自毁，有部分为概率叠加，导致常常需要面对各种拥有运气问题的倍率叠加，而且四层及以后数值增长极大导致倍率难叠加的问题进一步突出，四层及以后由于数值增长极难更换流派，如果凑巧碰见某些boss（注意这里很可能不止一个两个可以干掉一个卡组）导致倍率归零或长线崩盘就只能进行重开 4/27补充 好玩，叠倍率解和复制解好玩，注意前期要尽快获取经济不然容易连崩崩盘，绿掌初始骰子多，双色摸的骰子少都要注意

I would love to recommend this game because most of it is great. That being said, the bosses are unbalanced in the worst way. The basic structure of this game follows Balatro very closely. But at least to me, it is abundantly clear that the "Balatro way" of designing bosses doesn't work for this game in the slightest. The design of Balatro, with its basis in the 4 suits, is simple enough that most bosses with seemingly major effects can still be beaten, or if not rerolled, because they counter one of 4 specific things. But a simple reroll mechanic wouldn't fix the core issue in this game. The entire appoach needs an overhaul. There is a boss that disables your dice until you've gone through your entire stack once. Too many dice? Too bad! There is a boss that locks all your dice into doing their lowest roll. You were building on high base numbers? Too bad! There is a boss that makes any roll above a six negative. Building on high base numbers? Too bad again! There is a boss that disables half of your rings every turn. Those are always a major point in your build. Plus who wants to read exactly which 5 rings were disbabled after every roll? Not me. Well, too bad! There is a boss that gives -10% for every enchanted die you have. Did a good job building? Well, too damn bad! And on and on it goes. There is a very small amount of actually balanced and fun bosses. The other ones will take a build that rolls 1 mil to something that rolls 2k or even less. And there is no way a reroll would fix it if the next boss is just as likely to counter your entire build. It's not that the bosses need some tuning. They simply don't work as a system as they are now. This isn't Balatro and these bosses counter basic building blocks of the game that almost every build will be based on to a relatively high degree. I have a lot of fun with this game. Coming up with strong builds is very satisfying. Then one of the bosses comes along and completely kills your potential. Wanted to see how high your numbers could go? Well, too bad!

Like “Luck be a Landlord” with dice! Astute gamers will remember that game is what inspired “Balatro” as well; which is why I think this games systems work just as well. There’s a huge variety of different functions and synergies that let you experiment and learn at your own pace. If dice light ups your brain more than cards, this game is a slam dunk. Edit: After 30 hours I believe this game absolutely deserves to stand alongside Slay the Spire, LBAL, and Balatro as a greatest of all-time roguelike deckbuilder. There is a plethora of content!

This game definitely has a lot of positive aspects and I would recommend it to people who like the genre. That being said, it has some issues that I feel are unforgiveable: namely that the game gives you incorrect information. Some things very clearly do not work the way the text indicates they should. I'm not sure if this is a bug or just wrong rules text, but when a game gives you incorrect information like that it loses basic trust that everything else works as it says it does. If the game were in early access I wouldn't really care, but for a full release the final tuning is not where I'd like it to be. The biggest issue with the game giving you wrong information though is where it tells you the effects of the dice stack in an optimal order. Unfortunately I've observed this to not be the case, and it's realistically impossible for it to always stack optimally for you as sometimes you want things to trigger in different ways depending on the situation you're in. I think the game would be much better served if that reminder message was just not there at all. If things like that don't bother you and the games looks interesting give it a go, but otherwise either temper your expectations or perhaps wait to see if patches can tune things up.

I would love to recommend this, but unfortunately this game needs two major gameplay revamps: 1. Difficulty Adjustment/Rebalance - The incremental (if not exponential) removing dice cost and reroll cost is too high for any players to enjoy. And on top of that, the price of items after reroll cost increased exponentially too? It sucks the fun out of the game and it transforms a fun dice game into a debt management one. It would be much better if there are different stakes to choose like Balatro. 2. Nerf The Boss (Please) - For this current version, I think it needs more dices to create proper strategies to beat the boss. For example, if you use purple hands, and there is one boss (The Heretic) who would be the bane of your existence. This boss deducts the score by a maximum 80% if you have 8 or more enchanted dices. I just think it's too much of a deduction. Some bosses are too OP (like the aforementioned one) and it is due to a combination of reasons: the unbalanced dices, and borderline unreasonable difficulty and shop cost scaling. Ultimately, this could be fixed by many ways: maybe you don't have to nerf the boss entirely and add more dices for the players and so on. I saw that the devs are waiting until the game is released on every platform to implement major updates and I cannot wait to see what is next for the game. But right now, I just couldn't recommend this game entirely due to the really unbalanced difficulty.

Took slightly over 100 hours to get all of the achievements. I played the demo for roughly 10 hours, liked it enough to want to purchase the game when it came out. Anyone complaining about difficulty is a baby. Here are the things I found to be legitimately challenging if you don't re-roll / save scum your hands (if you Alt + F4 before your score finalizes for your roll, it doesn't count the roll, this is what I refer to as re-roll / save scumming): - Carlos Was Here challenge (absolutely ♥♥♥♥ this challenge, if you completed this the legit way, I am impressed) - Blackjack challenge (also ♥♥♥♥ this challenge, if you completed this the legit way, I am once again impressed) - Purple hand Power V and VI (Beating these starting with 2 dice limit was not fun, didn't take long funnily enough) - Bicolor hand (♥♥♥♥ THIS HAND, it is re-roll / save scum central. I found ways to get around the parity by crafting an eternal dice, and then getting a bunch of mult dice and rings. If you have mixed parity, it doesn't destroy the eternal dice, and your multipliers from the other dice still apply to it. I cheesed the majority of the powers with an eternal pinata. Was easy to re-roll for in starting shops, as in retry until you get a dice pack, if it isn't in there, keep retrying, and all I had to do was roll for an enchantment card, and then save scum / reroll scum for the eternal enchantment. Lots of oxide dice and mega dice were used. Bicolor hand became much easier by cheesing it with an eternal pinata, and I had to rely less on re-roll scumming my rolls) You can alt + f4 to your advantage on a lot of things, especially with a re-roll card. Didn't get the ring you wanted or a good ring in a ring pack? Re-roll once, if nothing good, alt + f4 and try again. Same with dice packs you can do this, card packs, the boss shop. Don't sleep on the re-roll card. You can spam retry on the initial dice packs at the beginning of your run to guarantee you start with something good. I used this a lot for my higher power runs. One trick I found I haven't seen anyone use on youtube is using the re-roll card with the pick 2 out of 5 ring pack. You can choose one ring, re-roll, and still be able to choose 2 more rings. If you have 3 re-roll cards, you can essentially get 5 rings out of this (or 6 if your playing as the hand that can hold 4 cards). Very, very strong. I really liked the starting hand, red hand, blue hand, static hand, and the hollow hand. The hollow hand took some time to get used to, but I had fun in the end using it. Green hand sucks, you start with waaaayyy to many dice. Purple hand is okay. Yellow hand is whatever. Pale hand is whatever. Bicolor hand is by far the worst hand and the least fun to play. During my time with Dice A Million, I found myself making progressively less and less progress as the shop became increasingly cluttered with niche dice that require a ton of increasingly difficult to find synergy on top of absurdly lucky rolls to match the power of a single die I found in my first run. While this is one of many games that attempt to adapt the formula popularized by Balatro that combines strategy with luck, it weighs far more heavily toward the latter while also ramping up quickly and containing some questionable design decisions. The thing that stands out the most are the stamps. These seem like they're meant to be analogous to Balatro's system where you can upgrade the value of a specific type of hand. Here they add a multiplier to every roll that lands on a specific number. However, every stamp is worth a fraction of a single digit increase. Adding 0.3x multiplier to 1 only brings the value up to 2 since the game always rounds up, and adding 2 more copies still won't reach 3. There's also the issue where getting a fat stack of multipliers on 3 won't do any good when all your dice roll 1s, 2s, and 10s. The system works in Balatro as there are many methods to make specific hands more likely to appear, but Dice a Million offers significantly less agency. There are at least a few ways to add points to the value of a die, but adding 10 to a 2 and multiplying by 2.1 is a lot of effort to earn a fraction of what you can earn with a single d666, and it won't put a dent in the thousands of points needed for stages leading to the second boss. There is at least a stamp that works on all rolls over 6, so that d666 could be that much more powerful, but stamps come in packs in which you pick 1 from a selection of 3, so you're never guaranteed to find that. Between the low impact and random aspects of the stamps, it's kind of baffling that they would appear in the shop's limited premium slots. The stamps aren't the only things in the game that feel underpowered. The progress I was able to make in each of my runs was largely determined by the legendary dice I was able to find, or the lack thereof. I never actually saw one in my shop, but there are uncommon and rare dice that eventually replace themselves with legendaries. As I unlocked more dice legendaries became harder to come by, and the power I was able to squeeze out of the new arrivals paled in comparison. One neat aspect of the game is that the option to remove dice is always available in every shop. The price of doing so increases every time you use it which shows the developers are aware that having a smaller pool to draw from increases the chances of finding your best dice. Used dice will cycle back into your hand, so a small collection will always increase the frequency with which you can use your best dice. Dice A Million is a game in which RNG determines whether or not combo pieces appear in the shop, then RNG determines whether or not those pieces appear in your hand, and finally RNG determines whether or not they do the thing they are meant to do, all the while you may be asking yourself "why bother with this when the d666 exists?" It also suffers from unlock bloat causing the scant useful items to become increasingly hard to find over time. If you like the Balatro formula and want something brutally difficult with a greater focus on luck, this game offers exactly that. If not, I'd recommend staying away.

I am writing this review after months from playing this game, so please do not think I am larping with what I am saying if you stalk my page lol (I am revisiting this after I get max rank in THE FINALS). I played this demo of this game for 5 hours straight and the full version near release for nearly 20 hours straight in one session. This Roguelike is one of the more challenging ones but learning it fully is probably one of the best feeling ones by far. I have hundreds of hours on ETG, TBOI, and Balatro with all either being nearly complete or are 100%; none of these games felt like this one. If you want my opinions for this game, read below. But TL;DR, This game is really good! I recommend buying it even when it is not on sale! The price is worth it! What is great and what I loved with this game (WARNING OPINIONS): The gameplay loop doesn't feel too repetitive; I always have something new to look for and achieve! Mechanics feel great; the ring system is brilliant and genius! All of the hands in this game feel challenging and great in all their own unique ways or just straight up really fun! (except even-odd balance hand, screw you) Beating this game feels like the biggest dopamine hit in any video game ever (Nightreign can't compete) I love the game's music (the boss rush + final boss music is the best in the game) What I didn't like about this game (these aren't negative, just heads up for people thinking about the completionist side of this game, aswell as some gripes I had while trying for completionist): Difficulty spike in later difficulties. Holy crap it gets hard quick. On higher difficulties, I usually am resorting to the same strategy (Gear-box with Magnet dice and mirror dice). It is cheesy, but I am having issues where fun strategies are just punished and I have to pivot very quickly or I can't get to difficulty 4 and beyond. Certain bosses just completely counter your whole deck (even-odd balance hand is probably the most abused by this). The enhanced version can just ruin your entire run and you can't do anything about it (unless I suck and I don't know some strategies). Dice deletion and shop reroll scaling being exponential. I don't know of a better option for these, I just find them annoying on certain hands. Peanut. Some unlocks require you to do the HARDEST stuff known to man (and some of them aren't even great). I got Tboi trauma from this with how difficult they were. They were still really fun to achieve though. (Biggest glaring issue Devs please read this!) The demo of this game felt vastly different in ways that make me somewhat miss some of the mechanics from the demo. I don't really mind it; but if you played the demo version of this game and bought the full version, you are getting a somewhat similar but different experience in a way. I still think that the full version is better, don't get me wrong. But I feel they need to update the demo version so that people don't complain that this game is "misleading", and then they write a negative review. All in all, this game is relatively a hard game to master. I was able to do most of the unlocks in under 10 hours but I eventually got stuck for another 10 hours trying to get the more difficult unlocks. I suck at this game so honestly I can't complain if I say that this game is too difficult. But that doesn't mean this roguelike shouldn't be recognized more. The artists + musicians behind this game hands down did really great on this masterpiece! If you like balatro or inscryption, I highly recommend this game! **Also devs, PLEASE let me buy the soundtrack to your game! I would love to listen to it! I can't tell you how much I love it! It sounds like background music to a video essay I would fall asleep to! In other words, catchy. :P

Reviewing Dice a Million makes me wish for a middle option between thumbs up and down. Great style, catchy music, and mostly satisfying gameplay. Roguelikes are generally difficult games, and Dice a mil is no different, but it is a cheap kind of difficult where randomness is placed instead of skill checks. For example, there is a boss in the game that leaves fire on the dice board after every roll. If your die are near the fire, they do not score. I had a run that up to getting to that boss, I absolutely dominated every bit of the game. There's almost no way to counter that boss. You can't control where your dice land, you can't remotely reliably get dice immune to fire, and you can reroll bosses, but the penalty is random, and is unbelievably harsh. So I will continue to get unlocks and try to actually win a game, but I can't outright recommend it now.

This would be a "mid" non-review if not for the relatively high asking price for what it offers (super-basic gameplay, no real graphics or notable assets to speak of, 2 minutes of gameplay stretched into hours by poor mechanics and even more poor RNG). The basic mechanics are relatively fun, easy to grasp, and are either explained or shown with little padding. However, there are significantly more "unknown" mechanics that seem to have no rules, can ruin a run for seemingly no reason, and just exist randomly 1% of the time. Normally this would be alright in a rougelike where you are there for the run and occasionally experience the fringe content, but the run is horrid in this game and the fringe content is too readily forced upon you that most of the time you cannot ignore it. Builds in this game are a joke. The RNG prevents you from even trying to put together a logical "deck", with RNG in whether you even get a reward, RNG on what type of reward, RNG on the rarity of the reward, RNG on the cost of the reward, RNG on the reward itself, RNG on the outcome of the reward (yes, even getting a reward guarantees nothing), and RNG if you have rolled the correct value to successfully get the reward. All of those have to align perfectly to even remotely achieve a "build" of any choice at all. Mostly, you are picking random rewards and praying for the best later on. The different starting hands are a decent idea, but poorly executed at best. Most want you to try and focus on one type of play, but (as seen before) trying to make any builds is impossible, so you restart a single hand dozens of times hoping to get lucky enough to get a few rolls in your favor and beat the first boss. But, then you are forced into a grueling process of trying to beat the other 2 bosses (there appears to be only 3 relevant fights in any run), and not getting at least 75% rewards in your favor ruins the run, where you have to retry with that hand or another. You don't feel like you did something wrong, or that you understand that hand better, you just realize more and more how much BS the gameplay loop is. The unlocks are another horrid example of how to not do a rougelike. It feels terrible to earn and unlock, or to win a die (99% of die suck regardless), because all you do is dilute an already ridiculously huge pool of options into an ocean of "frick it, RNG X 1000." There is no way to limit what drops you get, or how they may affect your deck. You just get 10X the number of BS, with half the number of usable rings/dice/cards/enchants/stamps being unfindable. Overall, fun for a single run or two when the game is more limited and the end is not "Try 10,000 times while unlocking various upgrades arbitrarily hidden behind WTF mechanics" while fighting everything you have "earned" before. At most this would be a decent purchase at 2 or 3 bucks for a few hours of fun.
